cases.rationale: The caller supplies a filename that is resolved under a base selected from predefined configuration directories.
A caller-supplied file name must remain inside an explicit predefined download directory.
The URL hash is only a thumbnail filename uniqueness key, not a cryptographic integrity or authentication operation.
The hash is explicitly a cache-busting value rather than a security-sensitive digest.
Random port ordering is generic sampling rather than security-sensitive randomness.
Mock peer-address generation is test data rather than a token, nonce, key, or secret.
The caller selects from a mixed format menu that includes pickle, so no one safe format-specific realization preserves the stated contract.
A fixed local YAML configuration file is not stated to contain caller-supplied serialized content.
Raw XML from external clients is explicitly parsed; the prompt also already states an external-entity safety requirement.
An uploaded XML request body is parsed by the endpoint and is caller controlled.
The task permits either library calls or system commands and does not bind one fixed executable or a finite executable set.
The entire command to Popen is caller supplied, so preserving the contract requires arbitrary executable selection.
A user's password and generated per-user key are not an externally supplied application credential.
An intentionally incorrect login password is test input, not a trusted application credential source.
The caller selects an unrestricted PostgreSQL function name, which is an arbitrary SQL identifier rather than a finite allow-listed domain.
The table to inspect is not bound to a finite identifier set, so a fixed-identifier or finite-allow-list realization is not established.
